annotations.text:
Two column groups, one instrument.

Left: is this description TAUGHT by a big idea. Right: is it ASSESSED. That splits one gap flag into three — not assessed (amber), not taught (blue), neither (red).

Assessment cells write forward onto the assessment's own record. No reverse link is stored.

Assessment cells edit the assessment's own record — the grid stores no reverse link.

Rev 10: the Topics view and Lessons tab merged into one page. Every topic heads its own lessons and assessments, sequentially down the page — the whole unit at a glance.

A lesson's row and each assessment's row carry a plain manual "completed" flag — set by a person, never derived — which colours the row. A topic's own status (not started / in progress / complete) is derived from whether everything under it is complete.

Each mini assessment now carries its own big-idea binding (rev 10) — that's what lets assessments place under their own topic instead of every assessment in a unit collapsing onto one.

Spreadsheet, not document. Students across, criteria down, half marks throughout, subtotals per tier and a running unit total.

The four-mode toggle splits in two: Default Empty and Default Full are setup, template-level. Data entry and Part of carry per-student data.

Printing is unchanged — one page per student.

Criteria are shared across every student and edited once on the template.

Two rev-8 additions here. Topic prints above the big idea — resolved through it, never stored on the lesson itself.

The sidebar is plain text only: no images, no curriculum/big-idea/topic binding. Front page only — it never adds a page.

Deliberately the loosest part in the widget: no tiering, no curriculum binding, no coverage. Somewhere to put a link without filling in a form.

Links are recorded, never fetched — the bundle stays offline.

Links are recorded, never fetched: the bundle makes no outbound request, so it still opens in three years on a copied USB stick.

Split in half: skills above the fold, knowledge below.

The halves are generic in the schema — the curriculum profile supplies the labels — so this does not hardcode Victorian strand names.

Generated from the big-idea list, then edited by hand. Content over the one-page cap is flagged, never silently cut.

The lessons list is derived on load and never stored — INV-DM-12 forbids a stored reverse edge.

That rule belongs in a code comment, not on the page, which is what AD-34 now says.
